seo.title: Supported databases
seo.description: The databases TablePro connects to, by kind: the query language, whether the driver comes with the Mac app or downloads, and which open on iPhone and iPad.

header.title: Databases TablePro connects to
header.lead: Native drivers for {count} databases, {featured} among them. Each row says what you query the engine with, where its driver comes from and whether it opens on iPhone and iPad.

relational.title: Relational
relational.intro: SQL databases with tables, keys and transactions. Several of them share the MySQL or PostgreSQL driver.

analytical.title: Analytical and warehouse
analytical.intro: Warehouses, columnar engines and federated query engines, where a scan costs time or money.

cloud.title: Cloud and serverless
cloud.intro: SQL services reached over HTTP with an account token, and libSQL files on your Mac.

document.title: Document
document.intro: Document and multi-model databases, each queried in its own language.

key-value.title: Key-value
key-value.intro: Keys and their values, read and written with commands or PartiQL.

wide-column.title: Wide-column
wide-column.intro: CQL tables partitioned across a cluster.

search.title: Search and vector
search.intro: Search and vector engines, queried through their own request consoles.

streaming.title: Streaming
streaming.intro: A log rather than a table: read and write messages with KafkaQL, TablePro’s own command language.

coordination.title: Coordination
coordination.intro: etcd’s key space, with leases and cluster members.

files.title: Files
files.intro: Databases kept in files that open in place, with no server to run.

drivers.title: How drivers are delivered
paragraphs: The drivers for {bundled} come with the Mac app and connect with nothing else installed.
Every other driver is a signed plugin that downloads the first time you pick its engine, before the connection form opens. That first download needs an internet connection.
Before a downloaded driver is installed, TablePro checks its SHA-256 checksum against the plugin registry and checks its code signature.
Plugins update on their own schedule, so a driver fix can arrive without an app update. A driver that is in use is updated after you restart the app.
The iPhone and iPad app has its drivers built in, so nothing downloads there.
